source: 2026 LCY EHS Dash Board.xlsx, sheet 'TRIR EXP.'
benchmarkSource: Bureau of Labor Statistics industry average, as stated in the source ('Bureau of labor Statistics industry avg.'); the industry (NAICS) and the BLS release year are not stated
notes: Annual history only. Monthly hours are never imported here; they stay in Safety Performance.
Years 2021-2024 have no monthly records: their typed annual man-hours (H15:K15) are the TRIR denominator for those years.
2025 and 2026 have monthly hours in Safety Performance and are calculated live from them. Their rows here are the workbook snapshot, kept only for reconciliation.
LCY TRIR 2021-2024 (H18:K18) are typed values rounded to 2 decimals (3.4 to 1). 2025-2026 (L18, M18) are formulas Recordable x 200000 / Man Hours.
TIR (L17, M17) is Incident x 200000 / Man Hours: an all-incident rate, not TRIR. It is kept as a legacy measure only.
Incident counts are blank for 2021-2024 (H9:K9). L9 (2025) is typed as 41, the same figure as the 2026 count M9 ('Incident Data'!N7); it is not confirmed as the 2025 count.
M15 (2026 man hours) is =Rates!M42, the sum of January-August 2026 monthly hours (145,194); the snapshot is therefore through August 2026.

years.note: Conflicts with the 2022 monthly table on the Rates sheet, whose hours sum to 425,039.90 with 0 recordables. TRIR EXP. (176,350 hours, 3 recordables) is used; the conflict is unresolved.
The Incident count 41 is a typed value equal to the 2026 count; it is not confirmed as the 2025 count.
Workbook snapshot through August 2026 (its man-hours are the January-August monthly hours). The 2026 benchmark repeats the 2025 figure; a 2026 BLS figure cannot have been published yet.
